title: Telemetry Schema & Simulation Playbook
author: Ravi Khanna
content:
Introduction:

This playbook standardizes a minimal telemetry schema for platform services and provides a set of deterministic simulation recipes used to validate dashboards, alerts, and operator runbooks. It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, dashboard authors, and operators running gamedays or CI smoke tests.

Intent and constraints:
- Reduce high-cardinality explosions and ingestion costs while preserving actionable signals.
- Provide reproducible traffic patterns to exercise edge cases (cost spikes, tail latency, cache storms).
- Define a safe rollout and deprecation path for schema changes.

Applicability:
- Applies to services owned by eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime: gateway, router, batcher, runtime-agent, cache-manager, prefetcher.
- Excludes customer-owned application telemetry and ephemeral debug-only diagnostics.

Required top-level fields (all events and logs must include):
- service.name: string, canonical short id (router, batcher, runtime-agent).
- env: string, deployment environment (prod, staging, test).
- request_id: string, correlation id for a request or synthetic transaction.
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC.
- tenant.id: string (or hashed token for PII-safe pipelines).

Recommended metric labels (low-cardinality):
- region: e.g. us-west-2, eu-central-1
- model: model-id (enumerated values only; do not include SHA or git refs)
- priority: high | normal | background

Minimal schema by signal type (human friendly explainers):
- Traces (OTel spans): include trace_id, span_id, parent_id, span.name, span.kind, duration_ms, status.code, attributes: {service.name, model, model.variant, batch.size}. Sampling recommended for high-throughput routes; always include at least 1 in 1000 of error spans.
- Metrics (OTLP/Prometheus): counters and histograms with job/service and enumerated labels. Provide buckets for latency up to expected limits (50ms, 200ms, 500ms, 2s, 10s).
- Logs (structured JSON): timestamp, level, service.name, event, request_id, tenant.id, msg, error.code (when present). Stack traces should be routed to a low-retention debug stream unless flagged critical.
- Token events (Kafka/stream): event_ts, request_id, tenant.id, model, model.variant, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, tokens_total, cost_usd_est, latency_ms. Token events are consumed by billing and cost dashboards; keep schema stable.

Cardinality controls and sampling: 
- Any label with expected >50 values must be sampled or histogrammed rather than indexed in metric labels.
- When introducing a new label, submit a cardinality impact estimate and a sampling strategy.

Alert and SLO mapping examples:
- Cost spike (P1): 5m rolling sum(cost_usd_est) for a tenant > 3x historical baseline AND ingestion lag < 30s -> page cost response oncall.
- Tail latency (P1): 99p latency for production router > 1200ms sustained for 10m -> trigger synthetic validation and initiate canary rollback if confirmed.
- Cache degradation (P2): prefix_cache.miss_rate > 25% with evictions/sec > 40 for 5m -> run cache-prefetch remediation and throttle noncritical tenants.

Dashboard engineering guidance:
- Group panels by signal: cost, latency, errors, cache-health, and routing. Each dashboard must include a time-shift comparison panel (7d) for obvious regressions.
- Provide a single interactive trace drilldown panel that takes a request_id parameter and opens the trace view.
- Keep high-frequency metrics to low-label cardinality; use aggregated summaries for long-term retention.

Simulation recipes (automated and operator-led):
Recipe A: Controlled cost burn (validate billing and alerts)
- Goal: ensure cost spike alerting, billing attribution, and runbook steps work.
- Setup: synthetic-client running in test namespace, kafka topic token-events-test, alerting rule deployed to test org.
- Steps:
  1) Baseline: `synthetic-client --broker kafka://kafka-test:9092 --topic token-events-test --rate 20 --model small --duration 10m --tenant test-tenant`
  2) Spike: after 5m, execute `synthetic-client --rate 1000 --model medium --burst 60 --duration 6m --tenant test-tenant`
  3) Validate: query token-events-test for request window, confirm cost_usd_est populated, confirm alert state and notifications.
  4) Post-check: run billing attribution smoke test and confirm synthetic tenant usage is recorded.

Recipe B: Tail latency degradation & canary lifecycle
- Goal: exercise canary detection and automatic rollback flows.
- Steps:
  1) Deploy model variant v3 to 5% via canary-orchestrator.
  2) Run latency-prober: `latency-prober --target http://router-test.internal/v1/generate --qps 60 --pattern heavy-tail --model v3 --duration 15m`
  3) Expectation: 99p latency rises above threshold and canary-orchestrator rolls back within configured 3m.
  4) Verify: check span samples with attribute model.variant==v3, confirm rollback logs and traffic reversion.

Recipe C: Cache miss storm and graceful throttling
- Goal: ensure cache prefetch/backpressure and tenant-throttling engage correctly.
- Steps:
  1) Warm cache with representative prefixes.
  2) Run `cache-stresser --host cache-manager-test:8080 --requests 20000 --unique-prefixes 8000 --parallel 100`
  3) Observe cache.miss_rate and eviction counters; validate automatic throttle of background tenants and prefetch policy activation.

Tool examples and invocation snippets:
- synthetic-client:
  `synthetic-client --broker kafka://kafka-test:9092 --topic token-events-test --rate 50 --model small --duration 600 --tenant test-tenant`
- latency-prober:
  `latency-prober --target http://router-test.internal/v1/generate --qps 100 --pattern heavy-tail --duration 900`
- cache-stresser:
  `cache-stresser --host cache-manager-test:8080 --requests 10000 --parallel 50 --unique-prefixes 5000`

Schema change and rollout policy:
- Additive, optional field additions: can be deployed with notification to #observability-changes; default is null and consumers must ignore unknown keys.
- Breaking changes (rename/remove required fields): require ADR in eng-platform/decision-records, 2-week review window, and 6-week dual-write deprecation period.
- High-cardinality label introduction: requires formal approval and a sampling plan; must include cost estimate.

Preflight checklist for telemetry changes (required):
- RFC/ADR link included in PR.
- Unit and smoke tests for schema parsing added to schema-validator.
- Dashboard queries validated against staging; smoke tests added to CI.
- At least one simulation recipe executed in staging and alert behavior validated.
- Rollback plan documented and operator contacts listed.

Alert testing matrix (owner & recipe mapping):
- Token cost spike -> Recipe A -> Owner: platform-ops
- Tail latency breach -> Recipe B -> Owner: runtime-sre
- Cache miss storm -> Recipe C -> Owner: cache-team

Operational guidance for oncall and dashboards:
- Suppress noisy alerts during scheduled experiments and annotate the alert with experiment_id.
- Provide a quick-action link from cost panels to prefill synthetic-client with tenant and time-window.
- Maintain a 7-day comparison panel when changing queries; revert to prior revision if anomalies appear post-change.

Examples and schema validation note:
- Example token event (single-line escaped JSON for schema-validator):
  `{"event_ts":"2026-02-28T15:22:10.123Z", "request_id":"req-7a8c9f", "tenant.id":"test-tenant", "model":"redwood-2b-q4", "model.variant":"v2-low-latency", "tokens_total":256, "tokens_prompt":32, "tokens_completion":224, "cost_usd_est":0.0048, "latency_ms":412 }`
